editorial_thesis: Build the interface, runtime boundary, portability layer, and consent model together—or the agent will be useful only in a demo.

topic_groups.title: Agent-Native Web + Runtime
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh Cloudflare agents-week material turns agent readiness, WebMCP, stateless MCP, and sandboxed code execution into a coherent platform lane; it extends rather than repeats the prior access-control coverage.

sources.title: Cloudflare Agent Readiness score
sources.why_selected: Use it as a Buildn/client preflight: score a public surface, then fix the highest-friction missing affordance instead of guessing what agents need.
sources.usefulness: The score is a heuristic, not evidence that an agent can complete a task end to end.

sources.title: WebMCP developer preview
sources.why_selected: Prototype a report or intake flow that exposes safe, typed actions rather than asking a browser agent to infer UI clicks.
sources.usefulness: Preview standards may shift; keep a thin adapter and explicit human confirmation.

sources.title: MCP v2 stateless core
sources.why_selected: Useful for portable client integrations where session affinity is a liability and tool calls need explicit state in payloads.
sources.usefulness: Statelessness moves context design into the application; it does not remove state, it makes it visible.

sources.title: Dynamic Workers sandboxing
sources.why_selected: A strong reference architecture for client automations: promote artifacts, cap egress, and discard mutable runtime state.
sources.usefulness: Sandbox boundaries, quotas, and dependency supply chain still need independent tests.

topic_groups.title: Developer Workflow Portability
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Visual Studio 2026 and GitHub’s September changes create a practical lane around BYOK, model/provider portability, agent telemetry, and repository safety—not another generic coding-assistant roundup.

sources.title: Visual Studio 2026 BYOK
sources.why_selected: A useful client pattern for sensitive work: preserve the editor workflow while routing data to an approved provider or local model.
sources.usefulness: Endpoint compatibility and enterprise policy are operational work, not a checkbox.

sources.title: VS Code agent usage metrics
sources.why_selected: Connect usage to accepted pull requests, review time, and rework; avoid counting prompts as productivity.
sources.usefulness: Vendor metrics are directional and may not capture quality or local tools.

sources.title: Actions cache-mode controls
sources.why_selected: Use as a concrete checklist item for agent-generated CI changes: caches can contain secrets and should follow least privilege.
sources.usefulness: Cache policy is only one layer; review workflow permissions and untrusted forks too.

sources.title: MAI-Code-1-Flash deprecation
sources.why_selected: Build model-change notices, fallback routing, and regression tasks into agent workflows.
sources.usefulness: A replacement may change latency, behavior, and cost even when the label looks similar.

topic_groups.title: Agent Research + Memory
topic_groups.selection_rationale: The September 11 arXiv stream exposes a neglected research lane: memory compression, temporal coherence, and criteria for defining agents. It complements recent research dossiers without repeating the prior formal-proof focus.

sources.title: Memory Compression for High-Fanout Agent Sandboxes
sources.why_selected: The idea maps to long-running client workflows where every branch should not carry the entire transcript or artifact set.
sources.usefulness: A title in the recent-submissions list is an early signal; inspect the paper before adopting its claims.

sources.title: Defining AI Agents: criteria and benchmarks
sources.why_selected: Use its vocabulary to separate “agent” marketing from an actual capability contract in Buildn specs.
sources.usefulness: Compendia are framing tools, not production validation.

sources.title: Memory in the Age of AI Agents
sources.why_selected: It offers a useful taxonomy for deciding what should be durable, editable, cited, or discarded in personal and client knowledge systems.
sources.usefulness: The survey is broad; implementation choices still require domain-specific tests.

sources.title: ResearchGym
sources.why_selected: A good pattern for evidence-first client research: constrain budget, preserve artifacts, and evaluate task completion rather than eloquence.
sources.usefulness: Research benchmarks can overfit tool interfaces and may not reflect live client ambiguity.

topic_groups.title: Privacy-First Mobile + Edge
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Google’s September Android Drop and the longer-running local/edge thread create a practical personal-leverage lane: useful on-device context without defaulting every task to a cloud transcript.

sources.title: September Android Drop
sources.why_selected: It is a consumer-scale signal that contextual assistance wins when tied to a narrow, visible job.
sources.usefulness: Availability varies by device, region, language, and account settings.

sources.title: Gemma offline deployment direction
sources.why_selected: This supports a Buildn principle: reserve local models for classification, routing, and private enrichment where latency and data control matter.
sources.usefulness: Local inference still has hardware, update, and quality costs.

sources.title: Firefox AI on your terms
sources.why_selected: A useful product posture for client-facing tools: make provider, memory, and permission choices legible.
sources.usefulness: Positioning claims need testing against actual data flows and defaults.

sources.title: Local-first software principles
sources.why_selected: Use it to evaluate whether an agent feature should degrade gracefully when network, provider, or account access disappears.
sources.usefulness: Local-first increases sync and conflict complexity; it is a design commitment.
